headline: MindEval2 reports guidance-calibration failures across mental-health support models
summary: An October 15 preprint introduces MindEval2, pairing psychologist-developed operational rubrics with MindSim, a longitudinal synthetic-patient simulator with cross-session memory. The authors evaluate 18 language models and report that guidance calibration—over-exploring, under-guiding or giving poorly matched advice—accounts for 60–88% of each model’s rubric findings; under-guiding rises from 12% of early replies to about 70% from turn 9 onward. The evaluation uses 50 synthetic patient profiles and a single GPT-6.1 Sol judge. It is a benchmark result, not evidence of clinical effectiveness or safety in patient care.
